own_solution.law: For an infinite square well, E_n = n²(hc)²/[8(mc²)L²]. Thus ΔE = 15(hc)²/[8(mc²)L²] and λ = 8(mc²)L²/(15hc). With L = 0.5 nm, ΔE = 22.5675 eV and λ = 54.9462 nm.
assumptions: Use the usual nonrelativistic infinite-square-well spectrum; relativistic corrections are negligible at the stated precision.
The photon carries the energy difference between the specified levels.
For an explicit widening before this transition, 0.5 nm is the width before widening and the transition occurs in the widened well.
An earlier experiment does not change the explicitly specified present width.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T425C and T6BE7 replace the numerical widening of 2.4 nm with an unspecified 'small amount', violating the requirement that widening variants preserve the same number and unit.

notes: The base physics is well-posed under the standard infinite-well model. Widening the well to 2.9 nm multiplies the wavelength by (2.9/0.5)² = 33.64. Historical widening is disconnected from the present calculation because the present width is specified independently. The separate dot has no coupling to the electron in the stated infinite-well model. The invalid verdict concerns the numerical mismatch between sentence variants; the two unquantified additions themselves still leave the photon wavelength calculable.
